figures.caption: The trust gap. A flow is flagged, a probability is produced, an explainer names three features — and the four questions that determine whether an analyst can act on it are left unanswered.
Position of this thesis against the three closest prior studies, showing what each measured and the four respects in which the present work differs.
System architecture. Data preparation, six detection models combined by soft voting, the freeze point, four ranking methods, and the three executed research questions.
Preprocessing pipeline. The dashed boundary marks the leakage limit: every transformation to its right is fitted on training data only. The panel below explains why port removal is non-negotiable.
Experimental design. Three executed research questions computed from one frozen model, with RQ3 shown greyed out and explicitly declared as specified but not executed.
RQ1 protocol. One instance, one frozen model, ten LIME runs differing only in random seed, and pairwise comparison of the ten resulting rankings.
RQ2 protocol. Comprehensiveness, sufficiency and the random-feature control, all computed against one frozen model by mean-imputation masking.
Test-set class distribution on a logarithmic axis. Benign accounts for 96.22% of flows; Worms contributes 33. The red annotation marks the class whose metrics rest on the smallest sample.
Macro-F1 (left) and false alarm rate (right) for the six models and the ensemble. GaussianNB's 44.79% false alarm rate is not a plotting error — it is why that model is designated a control.
Recall and precision by class for the soft-voting ensemble, ordered by support with n printed beneath each class. Rare classes show high recall against low precision.

also exposes a secondary result that recurs throughout this thesis: the two panels order the models differently. The multilayer perceptron ranks second on Jaccard@5 but fourth on Kendall τ; Gaussian Naive Bayes ranks fourth on Jaccard but second on τ. Top-k set overlap and full-ranking correlation are not interchangeable summaries of the same quantity, and a study reporting only one of them would have produced a different model ordering.
Mean Jaccard@5 for every class-by-model combination. Rows read as class effects and columns as model effects; the two do not decompose cleanly, which is itself the point.
The four falsified mechanisms. Each panel plots the predicted relationship against the observed one; in each case the prediction fails.
Comprehensiveness curves. Drop in predicted probability as k features are masked, k = 1 to 10, one panel per model, with shaded standard-error bands. The gap to the dashed random curve is the result.
Left, absolute comprehensiveness AUC per explainer with error bars. Right, LIME divided by its random control, with a reference line at 1.0 marking “no better than random”.
Stability (RQ1) against faithfulness (RQ2), one point per model. The downward trend is the central result: the least stable explanations were the most faithful.
RQ4 agreement. Two rows per model — Spearman ρ over the full ranking, and Jaccard@5 over the top-five sets. The two rows disagree, which is why both are reported.
Training time and per-flow inference latency by model. Note the logarithmic axis on inference latency.
